issues.description: Public API broken: Lucene99HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat.NAME and Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat.NAME demoted from public to package-private
issues.detail: These were public static final String constants. Code outside the package that references them (custom codecs, integration tests, Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, downstream consumers) will fail to compile. If the intent is deprecation-with-read-only, the constants need to stay public or be explicitly removed with a migration note. Silently narrowing visibility in the same patch that moves the class is the wrong shape.

issues.description: OffHeapQuantizedByteVectorValues fields demoted from protected to package-private while class remains public abstract
issues.detail: The class is still public abstract with public subclass DenseOffHeapVectorValues. Subclasses outside this package previously could extend it and access protected fields; now they can't see dimension, size, slice, etc. This breaks the extension contract. Either keep them protected or make the class final/non-extensible. Pick one shape.

issues.description: Deprecation annotation removed in the same patch that disables writing
issues.detail: Both Lucene99HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat and Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat had @Deprecated on them. The patch removes that annotation while throwing UnsupportedOperationException from fieldsWriter. Users get a runtime exception with no compile-time warning. Read-only legacy formats should be @Deprecated, not silently broken at runtime.

This diff does at least three things: (1) physically moves classes from core to backward-codecs, (2) narrows API visibility across many symbols, (3) disables writers with UnsupportedOperationException, (4) refactors test scaffolding into RW/V0/V1 variants. Each of these is reviewable on its own; together they obscure what is a mechanical move and what is a semantic change. THREE-PATCHES.

issues.description: PR description openly states the work is incomplete
issues.detail: Author says 'I have most of the logic moved, but there are additional things to figure out' and 'I don't think we can easily move Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorScorer just yet.' That is a draft, not a patch ready to land. Land the parts that are complete as their own diff with a clear scope; do not merge a half-move where the scorer is stuck in core but the format is in backward-codecs.

issues.description: Writer logic moved into test tree creates a load-bearing test-only class
issues.detail: Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsWriter is moved to backward-codecs src/test. That means the only path to write the legacy format now lives in test source. If anyone (including bw-compat index generation tooling) needs to produce a legacy index outside the test classpath, they cannot. State explicitly whether bw-compat index generation lives in tests; if not, this is the wrong shape.

The static import was changed from Lucene99FlatVectorsFormat.DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT to a new constant of the same name redeclared in Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat. That's a copy of a constant that already exists elsewhere. If the intent is to decouple from core, say so; if not, this is gratuitous duplication that future maintainers will diverge.

issues.description: rawVectorFormat downgraded from private to package-private with no caller justification shown
issues.detail: Visibility widened so the test-tree RW class can reach it. That's a smell: production code's encapsulation loosened to serve a test helper. Either inject the dependency through a constructor in the RW subclass or use a clearly named test-only accessor. Loosening 'private' to 'package-private' for test convenience is the kind of thing that quietly becomes a hidden API.

issues.description: numMergeWorkers / mergeExec constructor parameters now silently ignored
issues.detail: The constructor still accepts numMergeWorkers, mergeExec, validates them, but the fields are gone and fieldsWriter throws UnsupportedOperationException anyway. Either keep the no-op validation as a clear deprecation contract or simplify the constructor. Right now the code accepts and validates arguments it will never use, which is dishonest signaling.

issues.description: Commit message in CHANGES.txt is decent but the patch description in the PR is one paragraph of hedging
issues.detail: CHANGES.txt entry is fine. The PR description, however, doesn't tell the maintainer-six-years-from-now why the scorer is stuck behind, what the migration story is for users who set Lucene99HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat on their codec config, or how reads of legacy segments get scored without the original scorer being movable. Spell it out in the commit message.

issues.description: Test class renamed to V0/V1 without a comment explaining what V0 and V1 represent
issues.detail: Lucene99RWHnswScalarQuantizationVectorsFormat is renamed to V0, and a new V1 is added. The only hint is a one-line javadoc 'This is used to test an older version'. State explicitly: V0 = pre-bits version, V1 = post-bits version, with file format version constants referenced. Otherwise the next person to touch this has to git-archaeology to find out.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The mechanical move from core to backward-codecs is the easy part; this patch ships at least three things in one diff and the author admits in the description that not all the pieces are in place. The biggest concrete problem is silent API narrowing: public NAME constants demoted to package-private, protected fields demoted to package-private on a still-public-abstract class, and @Deprecated stripped at the same moment writes start throwing UnsupportedOperationException. That breaks downstream consumers at compile time and surprises remaining users at runtime with no deprecation warning. The Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorScorer being left behind in core while the format moves is a wrong-shape signal that should be resolved before this lands, not deferred. Split into mechanical-move, API-deprecation, and writer-disable patches; keep API surface intact where downstream code depends on it; restore @Deprecated; then resubmit.
